links.outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of native ChatGPT-4o patient education responses
links.effect: Native ChatGPT-4o mean FKGL 13.45 (university sophomore level), FRES 35.68, exceeding the recommended 8th-9th grade level for patient materials.
links.quote: In contrast, the native ChatGPT‐4o generated content with a mean FKGL of 13.45 and a FRES of 35.68, indicating a reading difficulty equivalent to the university sophomore level, which substantially exceeds the accepted readability thresholds for patient educational materials.

links.outcome: Readability and quality of AI patient education responses, fine-tuned vs native model
links.effect: Fine-tuned ACI Guide FKGL 9.25 vs 13.45 native; FRES 49.59 vs 35.68 (p<0.001); DISCERN 43.18 vs 35.29 (p<0.001).
links.quote: The ACI Guide achieved a mean DISCERN score of 43.18 ± 3.92 (range: 34–53), reflecting moderate‐quality responses, while the native ChatGPT‐4o scored 35.29 ± 5.0 (range: 23–45; p < 0.001), indicating poor‐quality responses.

unlisted_practices: Instruction-based fine-tuning and RLHF of an LLM to improve plain-language readability of patient education

links.quote: Similarly, the mean FRES score was significantly higher for the ACI Guide (49.59, range: 31–71, ±10.44) compared to the native ChatGPT‐4o (35.68, range: 27–48, ±5.08) ( p < 0.001), reflecting greater ease of comprehension.
The ACI guide had a mean FKGL of 9.25 (range: 5.80–12.20, ±1.64), while the native ChatGPT‐4o had a significantly higher mean FKGL of 13.45 (range: 11.40–16.20, ±1.30) ( p < 0.001) (see Figure 2 ).

unlisted_practices: Instruction-based fine-tuning and reinforcement learning from human feedback to improve DISCERN quality of procedure-specific patient education responses.
